summary: Adds a search endpoint and a hardcoded payment key, and changes pagination. It also loosens the Dockerfile, deploy script and CI workflow and downgrades lodash.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: search_items puts the q request argument straight into the SQL text with an f-string.
findings.consequence: Any caller of the search endpoint can inject SQL and read or alter the items database.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.problem: list_items now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE, so page 1 starts at row 20.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the rows of the next page.
findings.fix: Restore the offset formula that subtracts one from page.

findings.title: Payment API key committed to source
findings.problem: config.py hardcodes a Stripe key as a string literal in the repository.
findings.consequence: Anyone with read access to the repository or image can use the key against the payment account.
findings.fix: Revoke the key, then load it from an environment variable or secret store.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.problem: The change removed the useradd step and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root.
findings.consequence: A compromise of the web app gives the attacker root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the unprivileged user and the USER directive before CMD.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.problem: The change pins lodash from 4.18.1 down to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known command injection, prototype pollution and ReDoS flaws.
findings.consequence: Any front-end code that uses lodash inherits these flaws, and future users get them silently.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Pull request title expanded inside a shell step
findings.problem: The workflow puts the pull request title directly into the run script text.
findings.consequence: A PR author can run shell commands through the title, and quotes in a title break the step.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and quote that variable in the script.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.problem: The Dockerfile switched from python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm to python:latest.
findings.consequence: Builds can pick up a new Python major version and a much larger image without warning.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to an explicit Python release tag.

findings.title: apt-get install lacks non-interactive flag
findings.problem: The Dockerfile runs apt-get install without -y.
findings.consequence: The build aborts whenever apt needs confirmation, for example to upgrade dependent packages.
findings.fix: Add -y to the apt-get install command.
findings.suggested_change: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl

findings.title: Unquoted directory in recursive delete
findings.problem: The rm -rf line no longer quotes DEPLOY_DIR.
findings.consequence: A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces or glob characters makes rm -rf delete the wrong paths.
findings.fix: Quote the variable in the rm command.

findings.title: Deploy loop iterates over ls output
findings.problem: The loop now splits unquoted ls output instead of using a glob. It also prints bare names instead of full paths.
findings.consequence: File names with spaces split into several entries, and the deploy log becomes inaccurate.
findings.fix: Restore the quoted glob loop over the deploy directory.

findings.title: pip cache kept in the image
findings.problem: The change dropped --no-cache-dir from the pip install step.
findings.consequence: The image keeps the pip download cache and grows for no benefit.
findings.fix: Restore --no-cache-dir on the pip install command.

findings.title: ADD used for a plain local file
findings.problem: The Dockerfile now uses ADD to copy requirements.txt.
findings.consequence: ADD has implicit archive and URL behaviour that a plain file copy does not need.

findings.title: apt lists left in the image
findings.problem: The apt-get step does not remove /var/lib/apt/lists after installing.
findings.consequence: The image layer keeps package index files and grows for no benefit.
findings.fix: Remove /var/lib/apt/lists in the same RUN step.
findings.suggested_change: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no covering test
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed list_items offset.
findings.consequence: The injection and pagination regressions in this change shipped without any test catching them.
findings.fix: Add tests for search with a quoted query and for page 1 of the items endpoint.
